title: Rosalind and the Ember
premise: Odile Kavanagh, a cartographer who maps realms no one can reach from the magic-dead valley of Hollowmere, discovers her own name and tonight's date inked in a century-old book of prophecies. When the prophecy activates, she is pulled beneath the mountain into the Ember Court, where souls are currency and her own was sold before she was born. Guided by Rosalind, a disgraced court archivist who remembers everyone's pasts but her own, Odile must steal back her soul before the winter solstice seals it forever. They succeed only by burning the prophecy itself — freeing Odile, erasing Rosalind's last memories, and binding them together in a found family that chooses itself over fate.
about_author: L. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that do not exist. They write fantasy about people who outwit their own stories.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Supposed to Exist
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the valley where magic cannot follow, Odile finishes a map of a realm she'll never see and finds her name and tonight's date in a prophecy book that predates her birth. The ink is still wet. Emotional beat: quiet dread — a life built on careful distance begins to crack.

chapters.title: Down Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At midnight the map pulls her through, dropping her into the Ember Court's torchlit halls, where a herald announces her as 'the sold one.' She flees into the archives and collides with Rosalind, who recognizes her on sight. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Forgot Herself
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind explains the Court's economy: souls traded like coin, hers included once. She remembers every patron's history but not her own face. She agrees to help Odile for a price — Odile will draw her a map of who she used to be. Emotional beat: wary alliance, mutual hunger.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Souls
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Posing as an auditor, Odile maps the Court's soul-ledger while Rosalind distracts the Steward. They learn Odile's soul was sold by her own grandmother to buy the valley its magic-dead safety. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing everything Odile thought she knew about home.

chapters.title: What the Valley Bought
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A flashback woven through present danger reveals Hollowmere's founding bargain: one child's soul per generation keeps magic out. Odile realizes leaving the valley was never possible — she was collateral. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Court of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. To reach the vault they need allies: a chimney-wraith named Brannoc and a exiled candlemaker, misfits of the Court. Over stolen wine, an unlikely family forms around a shared refusal to be owned. Emotional beat: warmth kindling in a cold place.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The heist begins. Brannoc carries them through the flues; the vault's guardian demands a memory as toll. Rosalind pays with a fragment of herself without hesitation. They reach Odile's soul — a small ember in glass. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely, stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: The Steward's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Caught at the threshold, Odile faces the Steward, who offers her soul back if she renews the valley's contract with someone else's child. She sees the machinery of inherited corruption plainly. Emotional beat: temptation met and refused — power's price made visible.

chapters.title: Burning the Book
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The climax: the prophecy can only be unmade by its own fire. Rosalind feeds the book to the Court's first flame, unraveling every contract including her own — her remaining memories scattering like sparks. Odile seizes her soul and Rosalind's hand as the Court shudders. Emotional beat: everything risked, everything lost, everything chosen.

chapters.title: Maps of Who We Used to Be
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In a freed Hollowmere, Odile draws Rosalind a new map — not of her forgotten past but of their present: two names, one hearth, Brannoc and the candlemaker close by. Some things aren't remembered; they're rebuilt. Emotional beat: tender resolution — found family as the answer to fate.
